findings.title: One-sided termination for convenience
findings.explanation: Vendor can exit on 30 days’ notice at any time, while Customer must pay out the remainder of the term to do the same. This leaves Customer exposed to sudden loss of service with no reciprocal flexibility.

anchor.quote: Vendor may terminate this Agreement or any SOW for convenience at any time upon thirty (30) days’ prior written notice to Customer. Customer may terminate an SOW for convenience only upon payment of all fees that would have become due for the remainder of the then-current term of such SOW.

findings.suggestedEdit: Either Party may terminate any SOW for convenience upon ninety (90) days’ prior written notice to the other Party, and Customer shall pay only for Services performed through the effective date of termination.

findings.title: Short data return window, then deletion without notice
findings.explanation: Customer has only 10 days after termination to request its data, after which Vendor may delete it without warning. This risks permanent loss of business-critical records.

anchor.quote: Customer may request the return of Customer Data by written notice delivered within ten (10) days after the effective date of termination. Following such ten (10) day period, Vendor shall have no obligation to retain any Customer Data and may delete it in its sole discretion, without further notice to Customer.

findings.suggestedEdit: Within thirty (30) days after termination, Vendor shall return all Customer Data in a commonly used, machine-readable format and, upon Customer’s written confirmation of receipt, securely delete it and certify such deletion in writing.

findings.title: Unilateral fee increases
findings.explanation: Vendor may raise fees at any time with only 30 days’ notice and no cap, which undermines budget predictability over a multi-year term.

anchor.quote: Vendor may increase the fees for any Services at any time upon thirty (30) days’ written notice to Customer.

findings.suggestedEdit: Vendor may increase fees no more than once per Renewal Term, by no more than three percent (3%), upon at least ninety (90) days’ written notice to Customer.

findings.title: Vendor owns deliverables and models built from Customer Data
findings.explanation: Customer pays for the Deliverables but Vendor keeps ownership, including models and insights derived from Customer’s own data.

anchor.quote: Vendor retains all right, title, and interest in and to the Deliverables, its pre-existing materials, and any improvements, enhancements, or derivative works thereof, including any models or insights derived from Customer Data.

findings.suggestedEdit: Upon payment, Customer shall own all right, title, and interest in the Deliverables. Vendor retains ownership of its pre-existing materials and grants Customer a perpetual, royalty-free license to use any such materials incorporated into the Deliverables.

findings.title: Unrestricted use of derived data
findings.explanation: Vendor may use data derived from Customer Data for any purpose, including marketing. Combined with the narrow definition of Customer Data in Section 1.3, this data falls outside the Agreement’s protections.

anchor.quote: including any models or insights derived from Customer Data. Vendor may use aggregated and anonymized data derived from Customer Data for any purpose, including to improve and market its products and services.

findings.suggestedEdit: Vendor may use Customer Data, including any aggregated or de-identified form of it, solely to perform the Services for Customer.

findings.title: Broad, uncapped indemnification by Customer
findings.explanation: Customer must indemnify Vendor for any claim relating to Customer Data or use of the Services, regardless of Vendor fault, and Section 9.2 excludes this obligation from the liability cap.

anchor.quote: Customer shall indemnify, defend, and hold harmless Vendor and its affiliates, officers, employees, and subcontractors from and against any and all claims

findings.suggestedEdit: Customer shall indemnify, defend, and hold harmless Vendor from and against third-party claims to the extent arising from Customer’s breach of Section 7.2

findings.title: One-sided exclusion of damages, including data loss
findings.explanation: Only Vendor benefits from the exclusion of consequential damages, and it expressly covers loss of data, which is the main risk in a data processing engagement.

anchor.quote: IN NO EVENT SHALL VENDOR BE LIABLE FOR ANY INDIRECT, INCIDENTAL, SPECIAL, CONSEQUENTIAL, OR PUNITIVE DAMAGES, INCLUDING LOSS OF PROFITS, REVENUE, OR DATA

findings.suggestedEdit: EXCEPT FOR BREACHES OF SECTION 5 OR OBLIGATIONS RELATING TO CUSTOMER DATA, IN NO EVENT SHALL EITHER PARTY BE LIABLE FOR ANY INDIRECT, INCIDENTAL, SPECIAL, CONSEQUENTIAL, OR PUNITIVE DAMAGES, INCLUDING LOSS OF PROFITS OR REVENUE

findings.title: Liability cap limited to one month of fees
findings.explanation: Vendor’s total liability is capped at a single month of fees, which is far below market norms of 12 months and unlikely to cover a meaningful incident.

anchor.quote: SHALL NOT EXCEED THE FEES PAID BY CUSTOMER TO VENDOR IN THE ONE (1) MONTH PRECEDING THE EVENT GIVING RISE TO THE CLAIM

findings.suggestedEdit: SHALL NOT EXCEED THE FEES PAID OR PAYABLE BY CUSTOMER TO VENDOR IN THE TWELVE (12) MONTHS PRECEDING THE EVENT GIVING RISE TO THE CLAIM

findings.title: No data protection or security obligations
findings.explanation: The Agreement contains no clause covering security controls, breach notification, privacy law compliance, or a data processing agreement, despite Vendor processing Customer Data.

findings.title: Customer Data definition excludes transformed data
findings.explanation: Data that Vendor aggregates or de-identifies stops being Customer Data, removing it from the confidentiality and ownership protections that depend on this definition.

anchor.quote: excluding any data that has been aggregated, de-identified, or otherwise transformed by Vendor such that it no longer identifies Customer or any individual

findings.title: No availability commitment or service credits
findings.explanation: Availability is on a commercially reasonable efforts basis with no remedies for downtime, so Customer has no recourse for poor service.

anchor.quote: Vendor does not guarantee any specific level of availability, and no service credits or other remedies shall apply to any downtime.

findings.suggestedEdit: Vendor shall make the hosted Services available at least 99.9% of each calendar month, excluding scheduled maintenance, and shall provide service credits as set forth in the applicable SOW for any shortfall.

findings.title: Auto-renewal with long notice period
findings.explanation: The Agreement renews automatically unless notice is given 90 days before the term ends. This is easy to miss and can lock Customer into another year.

anchor.quote: unless either Party provides written notice of non-renewal at least ninety (90) days before the end of the then-current term

findings.suggestedEdit: unless either Party provides written notice of non-renewal at least thirty (30) days before the end of the then-current term, and Vendor shall remind Customer in writing of the upcoming renewal at least sixty (60) days before such date

findings.title: Conflicting payment terms
findings.explanation: Section 4.2 gives Customer 30 days to pay, but Section 4.3 charges interest after 15 days, so late fees would accrue before payment is actually due.

anchor.quote: Any amount not paid within fifteen (15) days after the invoice date

findings.suggestedEdit: Any undisputed amount not paid within thirty (30) days after the invoice date

findings.title: Confidentiality expires after one year
findings.explanation: Confidentiality obligations end one year after disclosure, which is short for business and technical information and may conflict with obligations Customer owes to its own clients.

anchor.quote: continue for a period of one (1) year following the disclosure of the applicable Confidential Information

findings.suggestedEdit: continue for a period of five (5) years following the termination of this Agreement, and indefinitely for trade secrets and Customer Data,

findings.title: Revocable, term-limited license to deliverables
findings.explanation: Customer’s right to use the Deliverables can be revoked and ends with the Agreement, so Customer could lose access to reports and models it paid for.

anchor.quote: non-exclusive, non-transferable, revocable license to use the Deliverables during the term of this Agreement

findings.suggestedEdit: perpetual, irrevocable, royalty-free license to use the Deliverables

findings.title: Re-performance is the only warranty remedy
findings.explanation: If the Services are defective, Customer’s only remedy is re-performance. There is no right to a refund or to terminate if re-performance also fails.

anchor.quote: Customer’s sole and exclusive remedy, and Vendor’s sole obligation, for any breach of this warranty shall be for Vendor to re-perform the non-conforming Services.

findings.suggestedEdit: If Vendor fails to re-perform the non-conforming Services within thirty (30) days, Customer may terminate the applicable SOW and receive a refund of fees paid for the non-conforming Services.

findings.title: Disclaimer of accuracy for an analytics service
findings.explanation: Vendor disclaims any warranty of accuracy, which may be unreasonable for a service whose core output is analytics and reporting. The disclaimer may be standard, so confirm against the SOW.

anchor.quote: INCLUDING ANY WARRANTIES OF MERCHANTABILITY, FITNESS FOR A PARTICULAR PURPOSE, ACCURACY, AND NON-INFRINGEMENT

findings.suggestedEdit: INCLUDING ANY WARRANTIES OF MERCHANTABILITY AND FITNESS FOR A PARTICULAR PURPOSE

findings.title: Narrow IP indemnity from Vendor
findings.explanation: Vendor only covers claims of U.S. patent or copyright infringement, excluding trade secrets, trademarks, and claims outside the United States.

anchor.quote: infringe a United States patent or copyright

findings.title: Asymmetric assignment rights
findings.explanation: Vendor may assign the Agreement to anyone, including a competitor of Customer, while Customer needs Vendor’s consent to assign.

anchor.quote: Vendor may assign or transfer this Agreement, in whole or in part, without Customer’s consent.

findings.suggestedEdit: Neither Party may assign this Agreement without the other Party’s prior written consent, except to a successor in a merger or acquisition that is not a competitor of the other Party.

findings.title: Force majeure covers events within Vendor’s control
findings.explanation: Labor shortages and failures of Vendor’s own subcontractors or hosting providers are normal business risks that Vendor should manage, not excused events.

anchor.quote: labor shortages, failures of subcontractors or hosting providers

findings.suggestedEdit: labor strikes affecting an entire industry

findings.title: Subcontractors without notice or consent
findings.explanation: Vendor can hand work, and potentially Customer Data, to subcontractors without telling Customer. Vendor remains responsible, but Customer has no visibility.

anchor.quote: Vendor may engage subcontractors to perform any portion of the Services without prior notice to or consent from Customer.

findings.suggestedEdit: Vendor may engage subcontractors upon prior written notice to Customer, and Customer may object on reasonable grounds within ten (10) days of such notice.

findings.title: Suspension on short notice
findings.explanation: Vendor may suspend all Services on five days’ notice for any unpaid amount, including amounts under good-faith dispute.

anchor.quote: Vendor may suspend the Services upon five (5) days’ notice if any amount remains unpaid.

findings.suggestedEdit: Vendor may suspend the Services upon thirty (30) days’ written notice if any undisputed amount remains unpaid.

findings.title: Low insurance limits and no cyber coverage
findings.explanation: Coverage limits are modest, and there is no requirement for cyber liability insurance, which is the most relevant coverage for a data processing vendor.

anchor.quote: professional liability insurance with limits of not less than one million dollars ($1,000,000) in the aggregate

findings.title: Vendor’s home jurisdiction
findings.explanation: Disputes must be resolved under Nevada law in Nevada courts, which is Vendor’s home state. This may be acceptable depending on Customer’s policy.

anchor.quote: governed by and construed in accordance with the laws of the State of Nevada
